## Section IV: Essay (10 marks)

Write an essay of between 225 and 250 words on any one of the following topics.

**A.** Describe a day in the life of a professional that you aspire to become. Imagine some of the successes and difficulties that you have encountered.

**B.** You are a careers counsellor for young students. Write a talk you are going to give on the importance of a chosen career.

**C.** Imagine that you are the mother of a young girl. She is about to choose a career. Write a letter to her, advising her on a career that will be useful to her as a person, a mother and a member of the family. Your name is Veronique Tenejou and your address is P.O. Box 65 Foumban, and your daughter is in Lycée de Deido, Douala.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
A personal letter in English always follows a fixed structure: the writer's address in the top right corner, the date below it, a salutation appropriate to the relationship with the recipient ("Dear Mum," for a close relative, "Dear Sir/Madam," for a stranger), an opening line that states the reason for writing, a developed body organised into clear paragraphs, a closing line, and a complimentary close appropriate to the relationship ("Love," or "Your loving mother," for family, "Yours faithfully," for a stranger) followed by the signature. The word count given in the instructions (here 225 to 250 words) must be respected closely: an answer noticeably shorter loses content marks, and one noticeably longer is not rewarded for the extra length and wastes examination time.

Only one topic needs to be answered. A full model answer is given below for Topic C, since it is the most tightly defined by the instructions (fixed sender, fixed address, fixed recipient); guidance for Topics A and B follows afterwards for candidates who prefer them.

## Model answer for Topic C (personal letter)

P.O. Box 65
Foumban

15th June 2000

My dear daughter,

I hope this letter finds you well at Lycée de Deido. I know you will soon have to choose the career you want to study for, and I wanted to write to you before you decide, so that you consider a few things that matter to me as your mother.

I would like you to think seriously about becoming a nurse or a doctor. I know medicine takes many years of hard study, and I will not pretend it is an easy path. But think of what it would give you in return. As a professional in health, you would never lack a way to support yourself, wherever you end up living. As a mother yourself one day, you would understand your own children's illnesses far better than most parents do, and you could care for them yourself in small emergencies. And as a member of our family and our community, you would be able to treat your brothers, your cousins, and our neighbours here in Foumban, which would mean a great deal to all of us.

I am not asking you to decide today. I only ask you to visit the health centre with me these holidays, so you can see what the work is really like before you choose.

Whatever you decide in the end, know that I am proud of you and that I will support you.

With all my love,

Veronique Tenejou

*(word count: approximately 230 words)*

### Guidance for Topic A (narrative essay)

Structure the essay in three clear stages: a brief introduction naming the profession and the setting of the day, a chronological body describing the main events of that single day (one clear success, such as solving a difficult problem at work, and one clear difficulty, such as a demanding client or a physically exhausting task), and a short concluding reflection on why this day confirms the writer's wish to pursue that profession. Keep verb tenses consistent (past narrative tenses throughout, since the day is being recounted as a completed experience) and use time connectors ("At dawn,", "By midday,", "Later that afternoon,") to organise the chronology clearly.

### Guidance for Topic B (talk / speech)

A talk addressed to an audience of young students needs direct address ("Dear students,", "you", "your future") throughout, rather than the third person. Open by stating the purpose of the talk, develop two or three concrete reasons why choosing a career matters (financial independence, personal fulfilment, contribution to society), each supported with a short example, and close with a direct call to action encouraging the students to start thinking seriously about their own choice.

### Piège à éviter
Do not mix formats: a letter must keep its address, date, salutation and complimentary close even under time pressure, and a talk should never drift into the third-person distance of a formal essay ("Students should think about..." instead of "You should think about..."). Examiners specifically penalise this confusion of registers between the three topics.

### Conseil
Count your words in blocks of fifty as you write (mentally marking where fifty, one hundred, one hundred and fifty words have passed) rather than only at the very end: this lets you adjust your pace in real time and avoid finishing at 160 words or overrunning past 280, both of which cost marks regardless of the quality of the content.

incertitudes: Le sujet demande de traiter un seul sujet au choix parmi trois (A, B ou C) : un modèle complet est fourni pour le sujet C (le plus contraint par des données fixes), avec des orientations méthodologiques pour les sujets A et B, plutôt que trois rédactions complètes.
